_doc: 08 §4.1-4.3 (merge, enhance, salvage) and 24 §6.1-6.2 (reforge, retune). 25 §7 E9/E10: MergeCrownCost and the +11 to +15 stone costs must be re-derived by the simulator with dungeons, events and guilds enabled together; do not pre-emptively tune them by hand.

enhance._doc: 08 §4.2. successRateBands gives endpoints ('85% -> 65%', '50% -> 25%'); the arrow is the document's ramp notation, so perLevelSuccessRate is those endpoints spread LINEARLY and evenly across each band's five levels — step -0.05 and step -0.0625. Every value is a function of two published endpoints and none was chosen for feel; the second band is non-integral by construction and is not rounded to look tidy.

salvage._doc: 08 §4.3. Merge Dust and the stone refund only: 24 §5.1's Set Token yield has no number here and no wallet row to move into, so it stays absent rather than guessed. The auto-salvage filter's rules are per-player configuration rather than tuning, so no default filter is authored. ROUNDING, and it is the game's one exception: both payouts here FLOOR, while every other whole-currency conversion in Core rounds to nearest (progression/minigame/run-reward scaling round AwayFromZero, the shop rounds ToEven in decimal). No document authors any of those directions. Salvage is the return leg of a SINK — it hands back part of what was already spent — so rounding it up would pay out material that was never paid in, and the stone refund would exceed the stone cost at some levels; the others convert authored REWARDS, where nearest is the neutral choice. Do not unify this one towards the others without a ruling on the refund ladder. Rules.Forge.GearSalvage carries the same note.

reforge._doc: 24 §6.1 — quality re-roll, keep-best, unlimited attempts. Mirrored in luck.json; this is the forge-screen view of the same numbers.

retune._doc: 24 §6.2 — affix re-roll with lockable affixes and a wishlist. No C-rarity row: C items roll no affixes (08 §2).

inventory._doc: 08 §5, as amended by the M4 retro's product-owner ruling of 2026-08-17. 🔒 CAPACITY IS FLAT: baseCapacity == maxCapacity == 1000 and nothing buys an expansion — 'I don't see a reason to increase the inventory size. It should be virtually unlimited, cap it by default at 1000 for now.' The same ruling explicitly did NOT add an EXPAND_INVENTORY row to 14 §2.3's vocabulary, so no command exists that could move the ceiling. This SUPERSEDES M4 kickoff decision 4 (320 = 120 + 10 × 20), which was [auto-accepted] — a conductor call, never the owner's — and with it 08 §5's 'up to 320' derivation from 10 §4. ⚠️ DEFERRED, NOT DELETED: 10 §4's Crown ladder (inventoryExpansionLadder / inventoryExpansionMaxPurchases / inventoryExpansionSlotsPerPurchase in currencies.json) and 10 §2's flat 400-Soul-Shard alternative stay authored, priced and UNSPENT, because the owner said they will 'potentially deal with the limit itself later'. expansionStep stays here as the forge-side half of the one quantity authored twice, and InventoryTuning.Read still cross-checks it against inventoryExpansionSlotsPerPurchase. What the reader now enforces in place of the old equality is the DEFERRAL itself, in two arms: the ladder's reach (baseCapacity + inventoryExpansionMaxPurchases × inventoryExpansionSlotsPerPurchase = 1200) must stay STRICTLY ABOVE the ceiling, so not one rung of it is buyable, and the ceiling must equal the base. Restore the pre-ruling numbers and the first arm fires; raise the ceiling without ruling on what may move it and one of the two fires. That is the loud failure the day a purchase command is authored.
